scope: Primary-source prior check for candidate43 supervision coverage, not novelty verification

papers.title: Probabilistic Anchor Assignment with IoU Prediction for Object Detection
papers.source: Paper Search arXiv metadata and download, version dated2020-09-05
papers.reviewed: Abstract, section2.2 and section3.1 anchor score/GMM/GT assignment description
papers.overlap: Model-dependent positive/negative assignment and replacing a fixed-IoU rule are established. PAA combines classification and localization loss scores and separates anchors by a two-component Gaussian mixture.
papers.difference_and_limit: Candidate43 audits already-emitted rows and the total reachable coordinate interval of a frozen postprocessor, not PAA or detector training. Reachability/uniqueness alone is not a demonstrated new assignment method; no superiority claim.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Anchor-based and Anchor-free Detection via Adaptive Training Sample Selection
papers.source: Paper Search arXiv metadata and download, version dated2020-06-20
papers.reviewed: Abstract, section3.3 and section4.1/Algorithm1: candidate centers, IoU mean+std threshold and multiple-GT conflict selection
papers.overlap: Positive/negative sample definition can dominate parameterization differences. Adaptive per-GT thresholds and resolving multiple-GT assignments are established, not innovation opportunities merely from applying them to tiny objects.
papers.difference_and_limit: Candidate43 is an annotation-assisted count of missed GTs reachable by zero-target rows within an unchanged residual interval. It neither reproduces ATSS nor proves deployable learning from those rows.

claim: A positive oracle only permits a low-cost ordinary supervision control. A distinct mechanism and matched-control evidence are still required before an innovation candidate.
